notes:
NEW STATE. Cliopatria has no Chichen Itza row; Later Mayan City-States 850-959 and 960-1259 (177,291 and 135,191 km2) cover the whole northern lowlands and Chichen Itza sits inside both.
DATES. Start 900 and end 1100 are the researcher's rounding of the page's 'between 900 and 1050 AD ... a powerful regional capital' and 'declined as a regional center by 1100'. The city was already prominent about 600 and its site layout dates 750-900; the state is drawn only for the regional-capital phase. The 1100-1221 gap before Mayapan is unexplained by any page: the Mayapan page gives the 1220s and 1221.
TERRITORY. No page gives an area or a frontier; the 100 km radius is a reading of 'central Yucatan to the north coast', soft. Puuc towns such as Uxmal are not mentioned by the Chichen Itza page (Uxmal is a separate city on its own page); Ek Balam appears only in an inscription that 'may mention' it.
TOLTEC. The page notes the Temple of the Warriors is 'analogous to Temple B at the Toltec capital of Tula', suggesting contact; no Toltec rule is stated and none is drawn. Spanish presence at Chichen Itza (founded after 1531, abandoned in 1534, ranch by 1588) belongs to later-mayan-city-states.
HUNAC CEEL. The chronicle conquest (1221, Mayapan page) is entered as a war in the mayapan dossier only, because it lies outside this state's 900-1100 life.
COUNTERPARTS. Yaxuna and Coba have no dossiers.
